strongest_angle: The geological formation of Chiricahua National Park 27 million years ago through massive volcanic eruptions from the Turkey Creek Volcano, creating extensive rhyolite tuff deposits and iconic rock pinnacles.

key_facts.fact: Some 27 million years ago, a volcano in southeastern Arizona unleashed a series of eruptions, strewing more than 1,000 times as much volcanic material across the landscape as Mount St. Helens did in 1980.
The rock pinnacles, columns, and balanced rocks at Chiricahua were eroded from layers of ash deposited by the eruption of the Turkey Creek Volcano 27 million years ago.
The Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), during their occupation here in the 1930s, named many of the prominent rhyolite formations along trails like the Ed Riggs Trail.
